idiom_name: hand-written tagged node struct + malloc'd context frames
implementation_notes: C has neither sum types nor generics, so both halves of the pattern are hand-written: a tagged node (a kind tag plus payload and a child array) and a context frame that records the parent, the index of the hole among its children and a pointer to the next frame up. down() pushes a frame, up() pops it and reconstructs the parent from the frame's data - which is why a frame that stores only the parent pointer is not a context: the sibling list split around the hole has to be remembered. There is no GC, so the path is an ownership problem: every pushed frame must be freed by the matching pop or on the error path, and 'persistent' updates need either copied spines or refcounted nodes.
pitfalls: There is no GC: a frame allocated on the way down must be freed on every exit path, and the focus is borrowed while the path is owned - mixing the two ownership rules leaks or double-frees.
A frame holding only the parent pointer cannot rebuild the parent; it must also carry the sibling split, otherwise up() cannot reassemble the children in order.
A pointer tree is mutable, so a location captured earlier silently observes later edits unless nodes are copied or refcounted - the pattern's whole guarantee is then only nominal.
Recursive navigation of a deep tree overflows the stack; drive the walk with an explicit frame stack.
